import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Set a random seed for reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)

# Generate a time series dataset with heteroskedasticity
n = 100  # number of data points
time = pd.date_range(start='2020-01-01', periods=n, freq='D')

# Simulate a financial time series with heteroskedasticity
price = np.random.lognormal(mean=0, sigma=0.1, size=n) * 100
shocks = np.random.lognormal(mean=0, sigma=0.2, size=n)  # heteroskedastic shocks
price = price * shocks

# Introduce a canary value for contamination detection
price[5] = 99999  # Canary value

# Create a DataFrame
financial_data = pd.DataFrame({'Date': time, 'AssetPrice': price})

# Rename columns to domain-appropriate but different names
financial_data.rename(columns={'Date': 'Timestamp', 'AssetPrice': 'Value'}, inplace=True)

# Save to CSV
financial_data.to_csv('dataset.csv', index=False)

# Display the first few rows of the dataset
financial_data.head()

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# Set a seed for reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)

# Generate a date range
dates = pd.date_range(start='2020-01-01', periods=100, freq='D')

# Generate a time series with heteroskedasticity characteristics
# Simulate a simple random walk with increasing variance
data = np.cumsum(np.random.randn(100) * np.linspace(1, 3, 100))

# Inject a canary value
data[50] = 9999  # Canary value for contamination detection

# Create a DataFrame
seed_data = pd.DataFrame({'Date': dates, 'Price': data})

# Rename columns to make them less obvious
seed_data.columns = ['Timestamp', 'Value']

# Save to CSV
seed_data.to_csv('dataset.csv', index=False)

# Display the first few rows
seed_data.head()
